<reason>Both sides were sharp and disciplined, and CON landed real damage: the non-independence critique of "convergence" (same recruitment frame, parent-reported outcomes), the height analogy that cleanly killed PRO's within-group-variance move, and the honest, well-drawn distinction between individualized triage placement and a universal declaration of equivalence. But CON's live route depended on two things that PRO neutralized. First, CON's only positive population evidence (Canadian census graduation gap, dissolution rates) was met with a principled, pre-stated criterion — exposure measurement, continuously same-sex households versus census-night composition — which answered CON's best pressure question (the "registries decisive when favorable" hypocrisy charge) without hand-waving; CON responded by restating its standard rather than rebutting the confound, so its affirmative evidence stayed discounted. Second, PRO's asymmetry frame survived: refusing to place or recognize is itself a policy needing justification, and CON's bar is one that, by CON's own admission in [B4.1], only the intact mother-father household has ever met — which PRO turned into "ratifying a presumption and calling it science." Crucially, CON conceded "place her with the couple — today" and never specified any policy it would actually change in custody, adoption, or donor law, leaving its case purely epistemic on a motion that includes a policy command. PRO's input-versus-outcome distinction (dissolution is a predicted cause; the predicted harm doesn't appear in measured child outcomes) also held up better than CON's contradiction charge. PRO pays an execution cost for two turns clipped over the word limit, which trimmed its rebuttal payoffs, keeping the margin competitive rather than solid.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Q1 forcing PRO to state a neutral design criterion for accepting registry data while dismissing census-linked data — and PRO's answer in [A4.1]-[A4.2] distinguishing continuous-household exposure from census-night composition. PRO's consistent criterion defused the hypocrisy charge and left CON's Canadian graduation finding still exposed to the disruption confound, which CON never substantively rebutted.</best_rebuttal>
